topDriver: Trump-Xi summit delivers: Hormuz joint statement + H200 China chip clearance + Boeing 200 jets = US-China tech detente fuels the AI trade and sends Dow past 50,000 for first time.
narrativeSummary: May 14 was the most consequential single session since April 30's record close — and it may ultimately prove more important. Four separate catalysts converged: the Trump-Xi Beijing summit, the Cerebras IPO debut, H200 China chip clearances, and strong April retail sales. The summit headline that moved markets most was Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent telling CNBC that China will use its influence with Iran to help reopen the Strait of Hormuz. 'It's very much in their interest to get the strait reopened,' Bessent said. 'China has a much bigger interest in reopening the strait than the US does.' The White House confirmed Trump and Xi agreed the Strait of Hormuz needs to reopen and that Iran should not be able to impose tolls on shipping. This is the most concrete third-party diplomatic pressure on Iran since the war began — China imports 10% of its oil from Iran and more than half from the Middle East, giving it unique leverage. Secretary of State Rubio confirmed Hormuz was discussed, with the Chinese side stating they 'are not in favour of militarising the strait' and 'not in favour of a tolling system.' Simultaneously, the US Commerce Department cleared H200 chip sales to approximately 10 Chinese companies including Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance, and JD.com — though no deliveries have been made yet due to Beijing guidance to Chinese firms to pause orders (exact reason unclear). Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang attended the summit in Beijing. Xi also agreed to order 200 Boeing jets. Cerebras Systems debuted on Nasdaq as CBRS, opening at $350 (nearly double its $185 IPO price), hitting $385 intraday, and closing at $311.07 — up 68% on the day. The company raised $5.55B — the largest US tech IPO since Uber in 2019, giving Cerebras a market cap near $70B on outstanding shares and $86B fully diluted. April retail sales beat expectations, adding a macroeconomic foundation to the risk-on session. The Dow crossed 50,000 for the first time. The S&P 500 crossed 7,500 for the first time. Healthcare +2% and Consumer Staples +1.3% led defensives, while XLK fell 1.5% — the notable anomaly in an otherwise broad rally, reflecting some rotation from tech momentum into value and defensives as the market digests multiple expansion.
macroStressSubtext: Trump-Xi Hormuz joint statement + China Iran pressure + H200 clearance drops MSI from High 76 to Elevated 64. Hormuz still closed physically but diplomatic trajectory sharply improved.
rateCurveRead: Yields eased modestly across the curve on May 14 as the Trump-Xi Hormuz joint statement and China's commitment to pressure Iran provided the most credible de-escalation signal yet. The 10Y fell approximately 4bps to 4.38% and the 30Y eased to 4.95%, retreating from the 3-year highs seen after Tuesday's CPI print. The 2Y fell 3bps to 3.92% as market participants reduced the most aggressive Warsh hike pricing — if Hormuz reopens, energy inflation resolves and the June 17 debate shifts from hike vs hold toward hold vs cut. The 2/10 spread held at +46bps. Note: H.15 May 14 official release pending; yields estimated from May 12 H.15 (4.42% 10Y) adjusted for today's session direction. The Schwab Market Update confirmed 'yields edged lower on China deal optimism.' Source: Federal Reserve H.15 May 12 official (May 14 pending).

drivers.name: Trump-Xi Hormuz Joint Statement — China Commits to Facilitate Iran Strait Reopening
drivers.linked: Brent, WTI, OGPI, hormuzclosurePct, China, Iran
drivers.source: TheStreet, CNBC (Bessent interview), NBC News (Rubio), White House readout, WSJ
drivers.detail: The most significant Iran-related diplomatic development since the ceasefire began. Trump and Xi Jinping met for 2 hours 15 minutes at the start of their two-day Beijing summit. A White House official confirmed the leaders agreed the Strait of Hormuz needs to reopen and that Iran should not impose payments on shipping. Treasury Secretary Bessent told CNBC: 'It's very much in their interest to get the strait reopened. I think they will be working behind the scenes to the extent anyone has any influence over the Iranian leadership.' Secretary of State Rubio: the Chinese side said they are 'not in favour of militarising the strait, and not in favour of a tolling system.' China's leverage is unique: it is Iran's largest oil customer (nearly all Iranian crude goes to China), and China's imports >50% of its oil from the Middle East. China pausing Iranian oil purchases would be the most effective non-military pressure available. hormuzclosurePct upgraded to 18% from 6%. MSI dropped to 64.

drivers.name: Cerebras CBRS +68% IPO Debut — $5.55B Raised, Largest US Tech IPO Since Uber 2019
drivers.linked: CBRS, AI hardware IPO wave, NVDA, OpenAI, AWS
drivers.detail: Cerebras Systems priced its IPO at $185/share (raised from $135 day before — itself raised from $125). On first trading day, CBRS opened at $350, hit $385, closed at $311.07 — up 68%. Market cap approximately $70B on outstanding shares, $86B fully diluted. Company raised $5.55B — largest US tech IPO since Uber's 2019 debut. Cerebras' WSE-3 chip is 58x larger than the largest GPU die. Customers include hyperscalers, foundation model labs, and sovereign AI initiatives. OpenAI $20B cloud deal (expires 2028), AWS deployment via Amazon Bedrock. Two billionaires minted. SpaceX, OpenAI, Anthropic IPOs anticipated later in 2026 — Cerebras confirmed the market's appetite.

drivers.linked: NVDA, China tech, H200, AI supply chain, May 20
drivers.detail: US Commerce Department approved approximately 10 Chinese companies — Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance, JD.com, Lenovo confirmed — to purchase Nvidia H200 chips. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang attended the Trump-Xi summit in Beijing. Morgan Stanley estimates $5-8B annual revenue upside from H200 China sales. Goldman Sachs forecasts Nvidia Q1 beat by ~$2B ($80.7B vs $78.8B consensus). Polymarket: 90% probability Nvidia beats May 20. Critical nuance: no deliveries made yet despite approvals — Chinese firms paused orders on Beijing guidance for unclear reasons. The approval creates the optionality; actual delivery timelines remain uncertain. Nvidia has ~700K H200 units in stock vs Chinese firm orders for 2M+ units.

drivers.name: Boeing 200 Jets + Xi 'China Will Open Wider' — US-China Tech Detente Trade Opens
drivers.linked: BA, trade policy, rare earths, China tech access
drivers.source: Fox News (Trump quote), TheStreet, Sherwood News
drivers.detail: Trump confirmed to Fox News: 'One thing he agreed to today, he's going to order 200 jets. That's a big thing. Boeings.' A 200-aircraft order would be worth $20B+ and represents China's most significant US aerospace commitment in years. Xi told executives attending the summit (including Musk, Tim Cook, and others) that China will 'open wider.' China also moved to pause H200 orders on Beijing guidance — the exact reason is unclear but may relate to the same tech-competition dynamic that produced the domestic chip subsidy programme. Xi separately warned Trump that mishandling Taiwan would cause 'clashes and even conflicts.' The tech detente is real but conditional.

risks.title: H200 deliveries stalled — Chinese firms paused orders on Beijing guidance despite US approval
risks.desc: CNBC reported that despite US clearance for 10 Chinese firms, no H200 deliveries have been made. Chinese firms paused orders on Beijing guidance — the exact reason is unclear. The approval creates $4-10B annual revenue optionality for Nvidia, but if deliveries remain stalled, it does not materialise as revenue. The gap between political approval and actual delivery is the key risk heading into Nvidia's May 20 report.

risks.title: Iran rejects Chinese pressure — ceasefire technically over per Iran, Hormuz remains physically closed
risks.desc: Despite the Trump-Xi joint statement, Iran's position remains unchanged — the ceasefire was declared broken after Qeshm Port strikes. Iran demanded sanctions relief, war reparations, and Hormuz control. China's influence is real but not unlimited. If Iran publicly rejects Chinese pressure or restarts military activity in the next 48-72 hours, the Hormuz reopening trade reverses violently. WTI could spike $10-15 in a single session.

risks.title: Cerebras valuation — $86B fully diluted at 168x 2025 trailing revenue is extraordinary
risks.desc: CBRS closed at $311.07, putting the company at roughly 168x its 2025 revenue of $510M on a fully diluted basis. Even with 76% revenue growth, extrapolating forward, the multiple assumes flawless execution for years. Customer concentration (OpenAI $20B deal expires 2028) and the first-year IPO return history (generally weak) suggest disciplined position sizing. The $385 intraday high vs $311 close shows volatility inherent in this valuation range.

risks.title: Nvidia May 20 — market consensus at 90% beat probability creates crowded setup
risks.desc: Polymarket at 90% Nvidia beats, Goldman forecasting a $2B revenue beat, pre-earnings positioning at +4.4% today — the setup for a 'sell the news' reaction is forming. The Palantir template (-7% on a clean beat at high multiples) and QCOM (-13.3% on no specific news) both illustrate the pattern. Nvidia needs data center >$45B AND Q2 guide >$50B to sustain the multiple. A $44B data center with $49B guide would be a 'miss' in the current pricing context.

risks.title: Xi-Taiwan warning — 'clashes and even conflicts' language signals Taiwan Strait risk remains elevated
risks.desc: Xi warned Trump directly that mishandling Taiwan could cause 'clashes and even conflicts, putting the entire relationship in great jeopardy.' This was a direct and unusually explicit warning delivered in a context of diplomatic goodwill — meaning Xi chose to send it despite the positive summit tone. Taiwan Strait risk is not priced by equity markets at current levels. Any Taiwan escalation concurrent with Iran would be a simultaneous shock to TSMC supply chains, China tech access, and global risk appetite.

strategies.title: Long the Hormuz reopening trade — short XLE, long airlines (DAL, LUV), consumer (DIS, RCL)

China importing >50% of its oil from the Middle East and virtually all Iranian oil going to China gives Beijing unique and direct leverage. If China's pressure on Iran produces a formal Hormuz deal, WTI falls to $80-85 within days. The Hormuz reopening trade: short energy longs (XLE), long oil-cost beneficiaries (airlines, cruise, consumer experiences). Disney, Royal Caribbean, Delta all benefit directly from lower jet fuel and petrol costs.
